23.english: Nouns that do not accept «Tanwin» ( ٌ  ). These are the names to which instead of «Kasra» accepts only «Fatha»
Unlike ordinary nouns, inflected words do not use «Tanwin» endings. Also, indeclinable words do not end in harakat «Kasra», that is, they do not decline into the genitive case.

According to the grammar of the Arabic language, nouns, in a certain state inflect into genitive with harakat «Kasra» at the end. For example: ( مِنَ الْجَامِعَةِ ) «from university». And, also in an indeterminate state can have «Kasra», when they are in «Izafet state» or if they are preceded by a genitive preposition, for example: ( مِنْ مَسْجِدٍ ) «from the mosque».
However, indeclinable words, unlike simple nouns, do not end in harakat «Kasra». In place of the genitive case, they have only the ending «Fatha» instead of «Kasra»
